title: Missions & Task Programming
contentStatus: Built per Content Principles (60% pass, terminology + notes). Mission interface specifics pending SME confirmation.

sections.title: From Awareness to Operation
learningObjectives: Understand the shift in responsibility from L1 to L2
Recognize what operating MoRo actually involves day to day
sections.content: L1 built coexistence and interface awareness. L2 is where you begin operating MoRo directly - assigning work, monitoring execution, and maintaining throughput. The fundamental unit of that work is the mission. Every task MoRo performs in a shift is structured as one mission after another.

keyTerms.note: MoRo's Human-Machine Interface (HMI) platform, used for fleet monitoring, mission control, and programming.

sections.title: What Is a Mission?
learningObjectives: Define a mission in operational terms
Understand the basic components of mission structure
sections.content: A mission is a defined task with a clear origin, destination, and completion condition - move from point A to point B, execute a handoff, follow a multi-stop route. The exact taxonomy of mission types available in ANT, and how they're categorized in the interface, is being confirmed with DiFacto's engineering team. The underlying principle holds regardless: every mission has a defined start, a defined objective, and a defined end state.

keyTerms.note: A defined task assigned to MoRo, with a clear start, objective, and completion condition.

sections.title: Assigning and Starting a Mission
learningObjectives: Understand the sequence for assigning a mission
Know the pre-checks required before assignment
sections.content: Before assigning a mission, confirm MoRo is in ready state (covered in L1-M3) and that the intended path is genuinely clear. Once assigned, MoRo executes independently - your role shifts from direct action to supervision. The specific screens and steps for mission assignment within ANT will be confirmed against the live system.

sections.title: Monitoring Execution
learningObjectives: Recognize indicators of normal versus abnormal progress
sections.content: Monitoring isn't continuous observation - it's knowing what normal execution looks like well enough to notice deviation. A mission progressing normally moves steadily and completes within an expected window. A stall, an unexpected pause, or a status that doesn't update as anticipated is the signal to check in. Most L2 operation is this kind of light supervision, not constant hands-on control.

sections.title: Validating New or Modified Missions
learningObjectives: Understand why new missions require validation before routine use
Know the general principle of supervised first-run testing
sections.content: Any new or modified mission should be validated before being treated as routine - run it once under direct supervision, ideally during a lower-activity period, and confirm it behaves end-to-end as expected. This is standard practice for any new automated process, not something specific to MoRo.

sections.title: When Missions Fail
learningObjectives: Recognize general categories of mission failure
sections.content: Missions can fail to complete for various reasons - a blocked path, an unmet condition, a system fault. Diagnosis isn't required at the operator level. The standard response: note what happened, assess whether it's safe to reassign or retry, and escalate if the cause isn't immediately clear. Detailed error code reference is covered in L2-M5.

questions.question: What defines a mission?
options: A defined task with a clear start, objective, and completion condition
questions.feedback: Correct. A mission is the basic structured unit of work MoRo executes.

questions.question: What must be confirmed before assigning a new mission?
options: Nothing - missions can be assigned anytime
That MoRo is in ready state and its path is genuinely clear
questions.feedback: Correct. Readiness and a clear path are the standard pre-checks.

questions.question: What does effective monitoring primarily involve?
options: Knowing what normal progress looks like to notice deviations
questions.feedback: Correct. Monitoring means recognizing departure from expected progress.

questions.question: Why should new missions be validated under supervision first?
options: To confirm expected end-to-end behavior before routine use
Only required for missions over 10 steps
questions.feedback: Correct. Supervised validation is standard practice for any new process.

questions.question: What's the appropriate first response to a failed mission?
options: Diagnose the exact technical cause yourself
Note what happened, assess safety, and escalate if unclear
questions.feedback: Correct. Operator-level response doesn't require diagnosis - note, assess, escalate.
